internationalElderlyRules.description: 国际老年人营销号专项检测规则(英语为主)

healthPseudoscience: big pharma doesn't want you to know

correctionMessages.healthPseudoscience: No supplement can legally claim to cure, treat, or prevent any disease (FDA/FTC). 'Miracle cure' and 'ancient secret' are marketing language, not medical evidence. Consult a licensed healthcare professional.
correctionMessages.authorityImpersonation: 'FDA-registered facility' ≠ FDA-approved. A white coat costs $20 on Amazon. Verify credentials through state medical boards. 'As seen on TV' means paid advertising, not endorsement.
correctionMessages.benefitScam: Medicare will never contact you unsolicited about new benefits. 'Free grocery/health cards' are common scams targeting seniors. No legitimate program requires you to 'call now' from a Facebook ad.
correctionMessages.supplementScam: 'All-natural' is not a legal term for 'safe.' 'FDA-registered facility' only means the manufacturing site is registered, not that the product is verified for effectiveness. 'Better than Ozempic' is an unsubstantiated claim.
correctionMessages.fakeDeadline: Legitimate government programs have standard enrollment periods, not 'act now' pressure. Urgency language is the #1 red flag for scams targeting seniors.
correctionMessages.deepfakeDoctor: AI-generated 'doctors' are increasingly common on social media. Check for: lip sync mismatches, unnatural facial movements, robotic voice, or the same 'doctor' appearing on multiple unrelated accounts. Verify any health claim with a real healthcare provider.
correctionMessages.cryptoScam: No legitimate crypto project will ask you to 'send crypto to receive more.' 'Double your investment' is always a scam. Blue checkmarks on X/Twitter can be purchased and do not verify identity. Never connect your wallet to unknown sites.

preventionTips.general: 1. Verify credentials through official medical boards 2. 'FDA-registered' ≠ 'FDA-approved' 3. Never give personal info from social media ads 4. Use ScamAdviser or TruthScore to check product legitimacy
preventionTips.benefitScam: 1. Medicare never contacts you unsolicited 2. No real program requires calling from a Facebook ad 3. Check .gov domains for real programs 4. Report scam ads to FTC at reportfraud.ftc.gov
preventionTips.deepfakeDoctor: 1. Look for lip sync mismatches and robotic voice 2. Search the 'doctor' name + scam on Google/Reddit 3. Real doctors don't sell supplements on TikTok 4. Check if YouTube/Facebook has labeled content as AI-generated
preventionTips.cryptoScam: 1. Never send crypto to strangers 2. Blue checkmark ≠ verified identity (since 2023) 3. Don't click crypto links from social media 4. Use ScamSniffer or similar tools to check wallet connections

elderlyRules.description: 老年人营销号专项检测规则

correctionMessages.healthPseudoscience: 不存在能治百病的偏方。任何声称「包治百病」「根治」的都是虚假宣传。健康问题应咨询正规医生，不要轻信民间偏方。
correctionMessages.authorityImpersonation: 正规医疗机构不会通过短视频/公众号推销产品或秘方。请检查所谓的「协会」「专家」是否真实存在。「华佗秘方」等历史人物名义的偏方均不可考。
correctionMessages.foodTaboo: 食物相克已被中国营养学会多次辟谣，不存在所谓的食物相克。食物没有绝对「不能吃」，只有量和个人体质差异。
correctionMessages.healthAnxiety: 这是典型的恐吓营销话术，制造焦虑后推销产品。正规营养补充应遵医嘱，不应被营销内容恐吓。
correctionMessages.forwardInducement: 「转发有礼」类内容是商业推广信号，利用社交链低成本扩散。正规健康科普不会要求转发扩散。
correctionMessages.extremeThreat: 「可能会失明/致癌/瘫痪」等极端后果声明是虚假恐吓的升级版。食物搭配不可能导致感官丧失或癌症。这类话术比「不能吃」更危险，直接利用恐惧操控行为。

preventionTips.general: 1. 看到「根治」「包治」「秘方」直接拉黑 2. 健康问题咨询正规医生 3. 帮家里长辈设置营销号屏蔽 4. 用营销号鉴别网页版/小程序检测
preventionTips.foodTaboo: 1. 食物相克已被科学证伪 2. 「不能吃」绝对化表述=营销号特征 3. 「可能会失明/致癌」=极端恐吓升级 4. 搜索相关辟谣信息验证
preventionTips.authorityCheck: 1. 核实专家/机构是否真实存在 2. 正规医生不会网上卖药 3. 「央视报道过」≠央视背书 4. 电视台传播偏方≠医学验证
